key_insight: MorphoStain uses physics-guided AI to separate overlapping Tau and amyloid-β staining in Alzheimer’s neuropathology, not cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support research quantification of Alzheimer’s pathology, but clinical utility is not established by the abstract.
method: Uses a latent diffusion teacher constrained by Beer–Lambert optical-density physics and guided by pathology foundation models.
Distills the teacher into a 0.12-million-parameter FastStudentU-Net for rapid inference.
Applies morphological routing to disentangle identical chromogen signals and estimates epistemic uncertainty.
evidence_signal: On 9,908 held-out SEA-AD patches, the authors report 40.56 dB PSNR, 0.9961 SSIM and 140.1 FPS, with significant gains over InverseAE and NMF (both p < 0.001).
watch_item: Identical-spectrum separation remains intrinsically ill-posed; reconstruction metrics alone do not establish biological accuracy or generalization across laboratories.
paper_title: MorphoStain: Physics-Guided Latent Diffusion and Morphological Distillation for Multiplex Stain Decomposition in Alzheimer's Neuropathology
